disease_label_per_paper: Familial Mediterranean fever associated with renal AA amyloidosis in a Korean child
presentation_summary: 8-year-old boy was referred with generalized edema for two weeks and sudden scrotal swelling two days before admission.
For one year before admission he had repetitive acute self-limited febrile episodes with elevated acute-phase reactants, without a clear cause despite evaluation.
Physical exam showed fever 38.4 C, blood pressure 108/75 mmHg, weight gain from 23 to 26 kg, pretibial pitting edema, and abdominal swelling without rash.

Labs showed CRP 140 mg/L, ESR 120 mm/hr, hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL, albumin 1.0 g/dL, fibrinogen 1029 mg/dL, and massive nephrotic-range proteinuria with urine protein/creatinine ratio 14.49 and total urine protein 12,297 mg/day.

After admission he developed abdominal pain. Imaging showed increased renal echogenicity, splenomegaly, small ascites, pleural effusion, bilateral kidney enlargement, lymphadenopathy, and minimal pericardial effusion.
Renal biopsy AA amyloidosis, MEFV variants, negative alternate autoinflammatory genes, Tel-Hashomer adjudication, and colchicine response are preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking context.

quality_warnings: Renal biopsy, MEFV variants, Tel-Hashomer adjudication, alternate-gene testing, and colchicine response are confirmatory/non-ranking.
The nephrotic presentation, edema, scrotal swelling, ascites, effusions, fever history, and inflammatory labs are retained as presentation evidence.
